title: Transferring prescriptions to a new pharmacy
context: You will hear a conversation between a customer and a pharmacist at a pharmacy in Coquitlam.

segments.speaker: Minh
segments.text: Hi, I hope this is the right counter. I just moved to Coquitlam from Surrey, and I'd like to move my prescriptions here, if that's possible.

segments.speaker: Ms. Kaur
segments.text: Sure, we can do that. Transfers are pretty simple. Which pharmacy are you using now?

segments.speaker: Minh
segments.text: Fraser Valley Drug Mart, on 72nd Avenue. I don't have their number on me, sorry.

segments.speaker: Ms. Kaur
segments.text: No problem, I can look it up. And what are the medications?

segments.speaker: Minh
segments.text: There's my blood pressure pill, I take it every morning, and there's a skin cream my doctor gave me for eczema. Oh, and the pain medication I got after my knee surgery, but I've almost finished that.

segments.speaker: Ms. Kaur
segments.text: Okay. The blood pressure pill and the cream, I can transfer, as long as there are refills left on them. The pain medication is a different story.

segments.speaker: Ms. Kaur
segments.text: That's a controlled medication, so the rules are a lot stricter, and we can't transfer it over. If you need more, you'd have to get a new prescription from your doctor.

segments.speaker: Minh
segments.text: That's fine, actually. I'm hoping I won't need any more.

segments.speaker: Ms. Kaur
segments.text: Good to hear. Now, how many pills do you have left of the blood pressure one?

segments.speaker: Minh
segments.text: Um, maybe four or five? I was going to refill it this week anyway.

segments.speaker: Ms. Kaur
segments.text: Okay, so here's the thing. We usually carry that one, but we ran out of the ten-milligram strength yesterday. I can order it, and it'll be here tomorrow after eleven.

segments.speaker: Ms. Kaur
segments.text: Is that alright, or would you rather our Lougheed location fill it, so you can pick it up there today?

segments.speaker: Minh
segments.text: Tomorrow's fine. I've got enough until then. Is there a charge for the transfer?

segments.speaker: Ms. Kaur
segments.text: No, there's no fee for the transfer itself. You'll just pay the usual dispensing fee when you pick it up. Can I get your date of birth and your Personal Health Number? It's on the back of your BC Services Card.

questions.prompt: Why does Minh want to transfer his prescriptions?

options.text: His old pharmacy has run out of his medication.
options.whyVi: Chính nhà thuốc MỚI hết loại 10 mg, không phải nhà thuốc cũ.

options.text: He has recently moved to a different city.
options.whyVi: Đúng: anh vừa chuyển từ Surrey đến Coquitlam.

options.text: His doctor told him to change pharmacies.
options.whyVi: Có nhắc 'doctor' nhưng bác sĩ không khuyên đổi nhà thuốc.

options.text: His old pharmacy is closing.
options.whyVi: Bài không nói nhà thuốc cũ đóng cửa.

questions.evidence: I just moved to Coquitlam from Surrey
questions.explanationVi: 'I just moved to Coquitlam from Surrey' = vừa chuyển đến thành phố khác. Đáp án B diễn đạt lại.

questions.prompt: Which medication cannot be moved to the new pharmacy?

options.text: The cream for his skin condition.
options.whyVi: Kem bôi chàm chuyển được nếu còn lượt mua lại.

options.text: The pill he takes every morning.
options.whyVi: Thuốc huyết áp chuyển được nếu còn lượt mua lại.

options.text: None of them, unless they still have refills.
options.whyVi: Điều kiện 'còn refill' chỉ áp dụng cho thuốc huyết áp và kem; thuốc giảm đau thì không chuyển được dù thế nào.

options.text: The medicine he was given after an operation.
options.whyVi: Đúng: thuốc giảm đau sau phẫu thuật đầu gối là thuốc kiểm soát, không chuyển được.

questions.evidence: That's a controlled medication, so the rules are a lot stricter, and we can't transfer it over.
questions.explanationVi: 'The pain medication I got after my knee surgery' + 'we can't transfer it over'. 'Knee surgery' được diễn đạt thành 'an operation'.

questions.prompt: How does Minh react when he hears about the pain medication?

options.text: He doesn't mind, because he expects not to need it.
options.whyVi: Đúng: 'That's fine, actually. I'm hoping I won't need any more.'

options.text: He is frustrated and asks to speak to his doctor.
options.whyVi: Minh không bực bội; anh nói 'That's fine'.

options.text: He is worried about running out of it.
options.whyVi: Anh đã gần dùng hết và hy vọng không cần thêm.

options.text: He plans to get a new prescription right away.
options.whyVi: Dược sĩ chỉ nói 'nếu cần thêm' thì phải xin đơn mới; Minh không định làm vậy.

questions.evidence: That's fine, actually. I'm hoping I won't need any more.
questions.explanationVi: Thái độ thoải mái: 'That's fine' và 'I'm hoping I won't need any more'. Đáp án A diễn đạt lại cả hai ý.

questions.prompt: What problem does the pharmacist mention about the blood pressure pill?

options.text: Minh has no refills left on it.
options.whyVi: Dược sĩ chỉ nói điều kiện 'as long as there are refills', không nói anh đã hết lượt.

options.text: It is a controlled medication.
options.whyVi: Đó là thuốc giảm đau, không phải thuốc huyết áp.

options.text: Her pharmacy is temporarily out of his dose.
options.whyVi: Đúng: nhà thuốc vừa hết loại 10 mg hôm qua, sẽ đặt hàng.

options.text: It is only available at the Lougheed location.
options.whyVi: Chi nhánh Lougheed chỉ là lựa chọn để lấy thuốc ngay hôm nay, không phải nơi duy nhất có thuốc.

questions.evidence: We usually carry that one, but we ran out of the ten-milligram strength yesterday.
questions.explanationVi: 'Ran out of the ten-milligram strength' = hết liều 10 mg; 'I can order it' cho thấy chỉ là tạm thời. Đáp án C: 'temporarily out of his dose'.

questions.prompt: What will Minh have to pay?

options.text: A fee for transferring the prescriptions.
options.whyVi: Dược sĩ nói 'there's no fee for the transfer itself'.

options.text: Nothing at all.
options.whyVi: Chuyển đơn miễn phí, nhưng vẫn trả phí cấp thuốc thông thường.

options.text: Only the standard charge for filling the prescription.
options.whyVi: Đúng: chỉ trả 'the usual dispensing fee' khi lấy thuốc.

options.text: An extra charge for ordering the pills.
options.whyVi: Không có phí đặt hàng nào được nhắc tới.

questions.evidence: No, there's no fee for the transfer itself. You'll just pay the usual dispensing fee when you pick it up.
questions.explanationVi: Hai ý liền nhau: không mất phí chuyển, NHƯNG vẫn trả 'usual dispensing fee'. 'Usual dispensing fee' = 'standard charge for filling the prescription'.

vocabulary.vi: chuyển đơn thuốc (sang nhà thuốc khác)
vocabulary.definition: to move a prescription record from one pharmacy to another
vocabulary.example: I'd like to transfer my prescription to this pharmacy.

vocabulary.vi: lượt mua lại thuốc theo đơn
vocabulary.definition: a repeat supply of a medication allowed by a prescription
vocabulary.example: There are two refills left on your prescription.

vocabulary.definition: a drug with extra legal restrictions, such as strong pain medicine
vocabulary.example: Controlled medications have much stricter rules.

vocabulary.definition: the amount of active drug in one dose, such as 10 milligrams
vocabulary.example: We ran out of the ten-milligram strength.

vocabulary.definition: the fee a pharmacy charges for preparing and giving out a prescription
vocabulary.example: You'll just pay the usual dispensing fee.

vocabulary.vi: mã số y tế cá nhân (BC)
vocabulary.definition: the ID number for a person's public health coverage in British Columbia
vocabulary.example: Your Personal Health Number is on your BC Services Card.

review.notes: Blind-solved all 5 Qs; key matched. Changed: pharmacist's absolute claim that controlled drugs 'can't be transferred between pharmacies' (federal transfer rules for controlled substances have changed since 2020) softened to a pharmacy-level statement; Q2 evidence/explanation and vocab example updated. Q1 option A trap wrong_speaker -> wrong_detail. PHN on BC Services Card and dispensing fee verified.
